summary: Essex County, NY fire tower on Pharaoh Mountain, built 1918 after a 1910 observation station; vandalized and removed by DEC in 1992; summit now public wilderness.

facts.design: 35-foot steel tower (Aermotor LS40 per Wikipedia) with a wooden observer's cabin and outbuildings
facts.status_note: Tower removed by DEC in 1992 after vandalism; no source read describes what remains on the summit

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia and the Forest Lookouts annual-report entry give 1918. A 1992 newspaper clipping says the tower was erected in 1917. The story gives 1918 and notes the 1917 claim.
Sources give a 35-foot tower (Wikipedia, Forest Lookouts). A 1943 Coast and Geodetic Survey description says about 40 feet. The record keeps 10.7 m, which matches 35 feet.

sources.title: Pharaoh Lake Wilderness
sources.publisher: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation

notes_for_editor: Wikipedia's body credits the Civilian Conservation Corps with erecting the tower in 1918. The CCC was founded in 1933, so that attribution looks wrong, and the story does not use it. No source read describes the summit today; the brief's gone status holds. Access is public per NYSDEC (wilderness trail), but the lookout itself is gone, so the public access applies to the summit only. Brief height 10.7 m is kept because it matches 35 feet. Spelling: the 1909 clipping and some reports use Pharoah; the state and Wikipedia use Pharaoh. Wikipedia also gives non-conforming status in the wilderness as a removal reason (no quote in evidence); the story mentions only its vandal-damage reason.
